sentences.text: The petitioner filed petition U/s. 22 of the Employee's Compensation Act, claiming compensation from the respondents, for the injuries sustained by him, during the course of his employment under the first respondent.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 29.02.2020 at about 8.00 p.m., when the petitioner was traveling as a cleaner in a eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093 along with first respondent who was driving the said canter, on Nice Road, towards PES college, near Rudresh Home, Kengeri,
Bengaluru, the respondent No.1 has lost control over the vehicle and dashed to a ongoing 407 tempo bearing No. KA-40-1214.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to P.M. Santhosha Hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as cleaner and getting income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue with his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, both the respondents appeared and filed their respective written statements.

First respondent admits that the petitioner was proceeding as cleaner in a eicher canter vehicle which was driven by him and he lost control over the vehicle and dashed against 407 tempo bearing No. KA-40-1214.
Further contended that the said vehicle was insured with second respondent and he had valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
He has denied that the petitioner is suffering from permanent disability.
Hence, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

Along with objections, the respondent No.1 also claimed counter claim by stating that soon after the accident the respondent No.1 has paid Rs.1,51,603/- to the petitioner for the entire medical expenses and other incidental expenses.
Hence, in case of allowing the petition, prays to refund of the said amount to the respondent No.1 along with the interest of 12% p.a.

The respondent No.2 insurance company in the written statement admitted the issuance of policy to the eicher canter bearing Reg.No. KA-41-A-7093 and the liability of this respondent if any, is subjected to the terms and condition of the insurance policy.
Further contended that, the respondent No.1 knowing fully well that, the driver did not possess valid and effective driving license and willfully entrusted the vehicle to the said driver.

Further denied the age, avocation, relationship of the employer and employee Chethana S.D. Allias Chethan vs Prashanth.R on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26706736/
2 between the petitioner and respondent No.1 and income of the petitioner.

sentences.text: The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he was an employee under respondent No.1?
2. Whether the petitioner further proves that he has sustained grievous injury during the course of employment under the respondent No.1?
3. Whether petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
4

. What Order or Award?
5.

One Chetan Kumar, who is working as Medical Records Officer at P.M. Santhosha Hospital is examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P13 to 16.
The petitioner has also examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW.3, through him Ex.P17 & 18 documents are marked.
First respondent examined himself as RW1., through him got marked Ex.R1.
Dr. Shabuz Biswash, Duty Doctor Incharge P.M. Santhosha Hospital is examined as RW.2, through him got marked Ex.R2.

Second respondent examined its official as RW.3.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
By considering the counter claim, the following additional issue is framed.

Additional Issue No.1;
Whether the respondent No.1 proves that he has paid Rs.1,51,603/- towards the medical expenses of the petitioner?
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Additional Issue No.1: In the affirmative Issue No.4 : As per the final orders for the following:-

Since these two issues are interconnected in respect of employer and employee relationship and the injuries during the course of employment hence, they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of the facts.

9. The petitioner to prove his claim produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, notice issued under Sec. 133 of IMV act aong with reply issued by the owner of the vehicle,
IMV report and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.
10.
The Ex.P1 to P7 are belongs to the documents of Crime No.28-2020 of Kengeri Traffic P.S.

The petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and filed evidence affidavit which is in consonance with the contents of petition wherein he alleged that while he was proceeding as a cleaner in eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093, the driver of the said canter caused the accident from which, he got injured.
11. In the same manner, the respondent No.1 who is the owner of the eicher canter bearing No.

KA-41-A- 7093 also filed written statement and examined himself as RW.1 wherein he also admitted that the petitioner who was a cleaner in eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093 and also admitted the fact of accident.
Both the petitioner and respondent No.1 have not produced any documents to establish their employer and employee relationship.
At the time of cross-examination the PW.1 and Rw.1 both answered that they have no documents to produce to establish the employer and employee relationship between themselves.
As per the PW1 & RW.1, the petitioner used to receive the salary in cash as such they cannot produce any other documents.

12. The petitioner even though not produced any other independent documents to establish that he is a employee under respondent No.1 his oral evidence has to be looked into along with the other documents produced by the petitioner.
Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on 1.3.2020 on the basis of complaint given by one Krishnappa who is an official working in NICE company who is the incharge of said roads.

In the Ex.P2 the informant informed about the alleged accident and also by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of KA-41-A-7093 and also injury to the cleaner who was in the eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093.

The Ex.P2 is given by the independent person who is not related to the petitioner or to the respondent No.1.
13.
In the Ex.P2 the informant informed the police about the injuries to the cleaner of eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093.
Further the Ex.P3 spot mahazar also established the nature of the alleged accident.
Ex.P4 & 5 are IMV notice and reply in which the respondent No.1 is shown as owner of eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A- 7093 and the petitioner is shown as cleaner.
The Ex.P5 IMV report also depicts the nature of damages found on the vehicles involved in the accident.
Ex.P6 is the head of the charge sheet in which the respondent No.1 is charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.

In the Ex.P6 charge sheet the IO has opined that the respondent No.1 being the owner cum driver caused the accident from which the petitioner who was in the eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093 as a cleaner has got injured.
The Ex.P7 is the wound certificate which also supported the case of the petitioner about the alleged accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Ex.P8 copy of discharge summary depicts the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

The Ex.R2 is the copy of MLC register extract wherein the nature of the Chethana S.D. Allias Chethan vs Prashanth.R on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26706736/

sentences.text: 14. In combined reading of all these documents no doubt that there is no independent documents or evidence is produced by the petitioner to show that he is an employee under respondent No.1.
The police documents established the fact of accident.

The Ex.P2 first information which is lodged by the person who is not connected with the petitioner or respondent No.1 has described the petitioner as a cleaner of eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093.
The respondent No.1 who is the owner of eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093 appeared and admitted that the petitioner was working as a cleaner in eicher canter bearing No. KA-41-A-7093.

Apart from this, the PW.1 also admitted that the medical expenses are paid by the respondent No.1.
15.
The respondent No.1 also claiming that he has paid the medical expenses.

Thus, by considering the preponderance of probabilities if the petitioner was not employee under the respondent No.1,
the respondent No. 1 is not going to pay the medical expenses.
Accordingly, no contrary evidence is adduced by the respondent No.2 insurance company.

By considering all these points, issue No.1 & 2,
answered in the affirmative by holding that the petitioner is an employee under respondent No.1 and he has sustained grievous injury during the course of employment under the respondent No.1.

Issue No.3:
16.

The petitioner to prove that he has taken treatment as inpatient examined one Chetan Kumar S., Medical Record Officer at P.M. Santhosha Hospital, Bengaluru, as PW.2 through him authorization letter, police intimation, MLC extract and inpatient records which are marked at Ex.P13 to 16.
These documents shows that the petitioner has taken treatment in P.M. Santhosha Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient.
17. Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre, Bengaluru,

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained compound fracture left distal radius and fracture of the right femur and he was treated with CRIF with IMIL nail.
Further PW.3 deposed that, total disability of the lower limb at 47% and whole body physical disability at 21%.

As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: The Ex.P16 is inpatient records wherein the line of treatments and the injuries sustained by the petitioner is explained.

As per Ex.P16 the petitioner sustained injuries to left wrist, right femur,
open fracture of left wrist joint and closed fracture of right femoral shaft and also wound on the left forearm near the wrist joint approximately measuring 3 cms.
20.

To prove the permanent disability, the petitioner examined the doctor as PW.2, Orthopaedic Surgeon who specifically spoken in his evidence that the petitioner suffers permanent total disablement of whole body is 21%.
There is nothing contrary is elicited from the mouth of PW.2 at the time of cross-examination.
The petitioner was working as a cleaner.

The points as assessed by doctor in the mobility and stability assessment along with the injuries mentioned in hospital records as the major injuries in the hands certainly the petitioner being a cleaner affected with his avocation and his disability may be considered at 20%.
21. As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for a period of 3 days.
The petitioner in his petition has contended that, he is working as cleaner and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
But he has not produced any document to prove the said fact.

22. Coming to the fact of quantum of compensation is concerned, the petitioner deposed that he was getting the salary of Rs.15,000/- from the respondent No.1 by working as cleaner in eicher cnater bearing No. KA-41-A-7093.
Even though the employer and employee relationship is established, the quantum of income of the petitioner is not established.
23. The petitioner produced Ex.P11- copy of Aadhaar card in which, the date of birth of the petitioner is 1.4.1991.
No other documents or evidence is available on the side of both parties to consider the age of the petitioner.
Hence, by relying on Ex.P11, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 29 years.
According to the Petitioner he was drawing salary of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But to substantiate this contention he has not produced any documents before this court and even the employer i.e. respondent No.1 has not produced evidence in this regard.

As per the Central Government Notification No.SO71(E),dated 03.01.2020 in which the monthly wages of a Employee as per Employees Compensation Act is considered as Rs.15,000/-.
24.
The doctor examined as PW.3 and assessed the disability of the petitioner at 21%.
Under Sec. 4 of Employees Compensation Act, the provision is made to calculate the amount of compensation.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner is not coming under the part I Or II of the Schedule I of the Employees Compensation Act.

sentences.text:
Hence, in the present case, Sec. 4 (c) (ii) is applicable and it states as follows:
4. Amount of compensation.- (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the amount of compensation shall be as follows, namely:--
(c) where permanent partial disablement result from the injury:
Chethana

S.D. Allias Chethan vs Prashanth.R on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26706736/
6 (i) in the case of an injury specified in Part II of Schedule I, such percentage of the compensation which would have been payable in the case of permanent total disablement as is specified therein as being the percentage of the loss of earning capacity caused by that injury; and (ii) in the case of an injury not specified in Schedule I, such percentage of the compensation payable in the case of permanent total disablement as is proportionate to the loss of earning capacity (as assessed by the qualified medical practitioner)
permanently caused by the injury;
In this case, as the injuries sustained by the petitioner is not mentioned in Schedule I the evidence of the doctor is placed very important role.
As discussed above, by considering the assessment given by the doctor, in comparison with the avocation of the petitioner, the loss of the earning capacity is taken at 20%.
As per section 4 of Employees Compensation Act while deciding the loss of income of an employee the court has to decide the relevant factor based on the age of the Petitioner.
As mentioned above the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was 29 years.
The relevant factor given to his age in schedule 4 of the act is 209.92.

As per section 4(1)
(b), 60% of his monthly wages has to be multiplied by relevant factor.
The 60% of the total salary of the Petitioner is Rs.9,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 60% =Rs.9,000/-) and it has to be multiplied by having reference to the percentage of disability and relevant factor.
Therefore the Petitioner in total is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,77,856/- (Rs.9,000/- x 209.92 x 20% = Rs.3,77,856/-) under the head of loss of future earnings/income.
26. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner is claiming that he has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards hospitalisation.
The bills produced by the petitioner is marked at Ex.P9.
The Ex.
P9 supported with Ex.P.10 prescriptions.
No doubt that the original discharge summary is not produced by the petitioner.
But he has produced the advance paid receipts which evidentiated that he has paid the amount of Rs.1,25,000/- in P.M. Santhosh Hospital.
By considering the same, the petitioner is entitle for reimbursement of the medical bills spent by him which are marked at Ex.P9.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under the heads of medical expenses.
As such, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,51,603/- under different heads.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.1,52,000/-.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

27.
Admittedly the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement admitted issuance of policy to the eicher canter bearing Reg. No. KA-41-A-7093.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.
28. Additional Issue No.1:
The respondent No.1 being the owner of eicher canter bearing Reg. No. KA-41- A-7093 contended that he has paid Rs.1,51,603/- towards the medical expenses of the petitioner.
No documents are produced by the respondent No.1 to show that he has made the payment.
But on perusal of Ex.P9 bill of P.M. Santhosh Hospital dated 4.3.2020, the total amount of the said bill is Rs.1,25,000/-.
At the time of cross-examination of PW.1- petitioner, the PW.1 admitted that the respondent No.1 has paid the entire medical expenditure.
The petitioner himself admitted that the hospital bill is paid by the respondent No.1.
Under the head of medical expenses, it is already held that the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the medical bills of Rs.1,52,000/-.
Out of which, Rs.1,25,000/- has to be paid to the respondent No.1, otherwise, the petitioner will be double benefited, which is not permitted under law.
Hence, it is just and necessary to order to release the amount of Rs.1,25,000/- which is the bill amount of the P.M. Santhosh Hospital in favour of the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, this additional issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:
29.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 22 of Employees Compensation Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,59,856/-
(Rupees Five lakhs fifty nine thousand eight hundred fifty six only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.

The petitioner was working as a cleaner.
Hence, by relying on Ex.P11, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 29 years.
The doctor examined as PW.3 and assessed the disability of the petitioner at 21%.
Under Sec. 4 of Employees Compensation Act, the provision is made to calculate the amount of compensation.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner is not coming under the part I Or II of the Schedule I of the Employees Compensation Act.
In this case, as the injuries sustained by the petitioner is not mentioned in Schedule I the evidence of the doctor is placed very important role.
Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
opennyai_summary.decision:
As such, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,51,603/- under different heads.
Out of which, Rs.1,25,000/- has to be paid to the respondent No.1, otherwise, the petitioner will be double benefited, which is not permitted under law.
Accordingly, this additional issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.4:
29.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 22 of Employees Compensation Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,59,856/-
(Rupees Five lakhs fifty nine thousand eight hundred fifty six only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount, Rs.1,25,000/- with interest shall be released in favour of the respondent No.1 on his proper identification and due acknowledgement.
It is further clarified that the compensation awarded under the head of future medical expenses shall not carry any interest.
Considering the quantum of award it is order to release the remaining entire amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
